text: The Fife Coalfield was a significant coal mining region in Scotland, primarily located in Fife and extending into neighboring counties of Angus and Kinross. Historically, it played a very important role in the economic development of Fife, providing employment for many years.  The first coal mine in the area was established in 1575, and the industry experienced rapid growth during the 18th and 19th centuries. At its peak, the Fife Coalfield boasted over three hundred mines, making it one of the most productive coal mining regions in the United Kingdom.  The Fife Coalfield began to decline in the early 20th century due to increasing competition from other energy sources. The last coal mine in the area closed in 1966, marking the end of the industry. Today, the Fife Coalfield is remembered as an important part of Fife's history, with numerous artifacts and monuments commemorating the industry. The Scottish Mining Museum in Newtongrange attracts many visitors, and the area is also home to several heritage sites dedicated to the coal miners of the Fife Coalfield.

text: Asparagus with Prosciutto di Parma Pecorino Pepato and Poached Eggs  Ingredients  -  1 bunch asparagus (about 1 pound) 6 large eggs 4 tablespoons unsalted butter 4 thin slices prosciutto di Parma torn into pieces 1/2 cup grated Pecorino Pepato cheese 1/2 cup heavy cream 1/2 teaspoon white pepper 1/4 teaspoon salt  Instructions Step 1 Bring a pot of water to a boil over high heat. Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with ice water and set aside. Cut the tips off the asparagus and set aside. Cut the stalks into 1-inch pieces and set aside. Blanch the tips in the boiling water for 1 minute. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the tips to the ice water and chill for 1 minute. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. Blanch the stalks for 4 to 6 minutes or until tender. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. Step 2 Crack the eggs into individual ramekins or cups. Fill a large skillet with water and add the white vinegar. Bring the water to a simmer over medium heat. Carefully slide the eggs into the water and cook for 3 to 5 minutes or until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked as desired. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the eggs to a towel to drain. Step 3 Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the prosciutto and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until the ham is crisp. Add the asparagus and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until tender-crisp. Add the cheese and cook for 1 minute or until melted. Stir in the heavy cream, pepper and salt and cook for 1 minute or until heated through. Step 4 To serve, divide the asparagus and prosciutto among individual plates. Top each with a poached egg and some of the cheese sauce.  Nutrition Facts Calories, three hundred eighty-three Fat, 29g Cholesterol, 443mg Sodium, 1152mg Carbs, 6g Fiber, 1g Sugars, 3g Protein, 23g

text: Barry Holmes triumphs in comeback victory  Barry Holmes secured a stunning comeback to win the Welsh Open snooker title in Cardiff. The world number 39 trailed 6-2 to Mark Selby in the final but won eight of the next nine frames to triumph 10-7.  It is the first ranking event success for the 41-year old from Birmingham who has now earned £200,000 in prize money this season.  "I'm over the moon it's been a great week," Holmes said. "I've been working hard on my game and it's nice to get some reward for it."  Selby, the world number two, had been in dominant form throughout the tournament and looked on course for victory when he moved 6-2 ahead. But Holmes, who had earlier in the week knocked out world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan in the last 16, showed great character to hit back.  He levelled at 6-6 with a break of one hundred six and then took the lead for the first time in the match with a run of 70. Selby responded with a break of 77 to make it 7-7, but Holmes took the next three frames moving forward with within one of victory.  The Leicester player then had a chance to force a decider in the 17th frame, but missed a red with the rest when on 46; Holmes made no mistake with a break of 53 to secure the title.  "I'm gutted to lose but I've got to take my hat off to Barry, he played unbelievable," Selby said. "I had my chances in the match, but I couldn't take them. I'm sure I'll be back stronger for it."
